meta.geography_note: GEOGRAPHY. 'Central Los Angeles' has no single official statistical definition. This report therefore uses three nested OFFICIAL geographies and one official planning geography: (1) City of Los Angeles (Census place, FIPS 0644000); (2) Los Angeles County (FIPS 06037); (3) Los Angeles-Long Beach-Anaheim MSA / Los Angeles-Long Beach-Glendale Metropolitan Division; and (4) the City of Los Angeles Downtown (Central City + Central City North) Community Plan Area, the official City planning unit that covers central Los Angeles. Parcel-level micro-geography is deliberately NOT filled in, because the property address is withheld under the privacy protocol.

rows.s: Southern California Association of Governments (SCAG), Demographics & Growth Forecast Technical Report
rows.n: SCAG is the federally designated metropolitan planning organization for the region. HOUSEHOLDS are forecast to grow +21.5% by 2035 even while population declines — smaller households, more of them. This is the single most important demand signal for a drive-thru QSR site.

rows.m: Central City Community Plan Area — land area
rows.s: City of Los Angeles Department of City Planning
rows.n: Official City planning geography: bounded north by Sunset Boulevard / Cesar Chavez Avenue, south by the Santa Monica Freeway (I-10), west by the Harbor Freeway (I-110), east by Alameda Street.

rows.m: Central City North Community Plan Area — land area
rows.s: City of Los Angeles Department of City Planning
rows.n: Bounded north by Stadium Way / Lilac Terrace / North Broadway, south by the City of Vernon, west by Alameda Street, east by the Los Angeles River.

rows.m: Downtown Community Plan — planning horizon
rows.s: City of Los Angeles Department of City Planning
rows.n: Consolidates Central City + Central City North into one Downtown Community Plan Area. The 2040 horizon sits inside the 2030-2035 lease-expiry decision window.
